observations.content:
Summary: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, as stated by multiple sources including Wikipedia, Britannica, and the National Capital Authority. It is located in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) and was chosen as the capital in 1908. The city was officially named Canberra in 1913 and is an entirely planned city designed by American architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin. The federal Parliament's official transfer from Melbourne to Canberra occurred on May 9, 1927.

    Canberra (/ˈkænbrə/ ⓘ KAN-brə; Ngunawal: Kanbarra) is the capital city of Australia and the largest population centre in the Australian Capital Territory. With an estimated population of 484,630 as of 2025, Canberra is Australia's largest inland city and the eighth-largest Australian city by population. The city occupies most of the northern quadrant of the Australian Capital Territory, and its urban sprawl borders the state of New South Wales to the northwest, northeast and southeast.     https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra
    The capital of the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) is Canberra. Canberra sits on the Molonglo River roughly 150 miles southwest of Sydney. In 1909, the site was chosen as the location for the new capital, and the ACT's delineation followed. Construction began in 1913, but was interrupted by World War I. The federal Parliament's official transfer from Melbourne to the new capital occurred on May 9, 1927. [...] In 1908, the Canberra-Yass district was chosen as the capital site. In 1911, the federal government began acquiring land for the city, which has remained under government ownership. Construction was interrupted by World War I but resumed afterward, and the first Parliament House opened in 1927, when the population neared 6,000. Today, the ACT is home to Canberra, the national capital, and numerous conservation areas.
